newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN CATERPILLAR WORKERS REJECT CUTS.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN CATERPILLAR WORKERS REJECT CUTS.

text.p: Workers at the Belgian unit of U.S. moving equipment maker Caterpillar rejected a billion franc cost cutting plan and now stand to incur tough management measures to end the long-running dispute.

The results of a referendum held earlier this week and announced on Friday showed 79 percent of staff rejected the plan, 20 percent were in favour and one percent cast blank votes or their ballots were void, union sources said.
Spokesman Antonio Cocciole of the FGTB union called the referendum a success.
In an initial statement Caterpillar management said it regretted the outcome. It expected to meet the unions on November 14 to hear what steps the unions would take next.
Earlier this week Caterpillar said that if its plan were rejected there might be sackings, investment in the plant could be halted and parts of the operation might be moved elsewhere.
The plan is to boost competitiveness, includes voluntary early retirement, and aims to achieve 1.8 billion francs of economies over five years, of which savings of 300 million on wages.
Caterpillar staff has been on strike for over 40 days and three attempts at arbitration have failed.
The plant currently employs some 2,500 blue-collar workers and 1,000 white-collar.
